title: Synergistic Action and Style Priors for Learning Legged Locomotion
abstract: arXiv:2410.03246v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) enables robots to learn complex behaviors through interaction with the environment. However, due to the unrestricted nature of the learning algorithms, the resulting solutions are often brittle and appear unnatural. This is especially true for learning direct joint-level torque control, as inductive biases are difficult to integrate into the learning process. We propose an inductive bias for learning locomotion that is especially useful for torque control: latent actions learned from a small dataset of expert demonstrations. This prior allows the policy to directly leverage knowledge contained in the expert's actions and facilitates more efficient exploration. We observe that the agent is not restricted to the reward levels of the demonstration, and performance in transfer tasks is improved significantly. translated_title: 面向足式运动学习的协同动作与风格先验
translated_abstract: 深度强化学习（DRL）使机器人能够通过与环境的交互来学习复杂行为。然而，由于学习算法本身缺乏约束，所得到的解决方案往往脆弱且显得不自然。在学习直接的关节级力矩控制时尤其如此，因为归纳偏置难以融入学习过程。我们提出了一种用于学习运动能力的归纳偏置，该方法对力矩控制尤为有效：从小型专家演示数据集中学习到的潜在动作先验。这种先验使策略能够直接利用专家动作中蕴含的知识，并促进更高效的探索。我们观察到，智能体并不受限于演示所达到的奖励水平，且在迁移任务中的性能得到显著提升。将潜在动作先验与风格奖励相结合进行模仿，能够更接近地复现演示中的行为。
tldr: 该论文提出将从专家演示中学习到的潜在动作先验与风格奖励相结合，作为足式机器人力矩控制学习的归纳偏置，从而实现更自然的运动行为并显著提升迁移任务性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes combining latent action priors learned from expert demonstrations with style rewards as an inductive bias for torque-controlled legged locomotion, enabling more natural behaviors and significantly improved transfer task performance.
